mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 months compresses discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as equity valuations re-rate upward.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% over 3 months signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates weakening demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline, SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing slowdown regime (INDPRO < 100), a decline in industrial production signals reduced output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 320 for two consecutive months signals persistent inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days as central bank delays rate cuts.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 320, SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) by >0.5% MoM signals broad economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In instances where both PAYEMS and INDPRO decline >0.5% MoM, SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market contraction regime (HOUST < 1250), a decline in housing starts causes negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as consumer confidence weakens.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1250, SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) over 3 months signals stronger economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS increases for 3 months, SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of cases.
